title: On-Prem Residency Safeguard Policy Generator & Regional Failover Constraints
creator: Clara Nguyen
description: Build a deterministic, auditable policy generator and enforcement layer for Private/VPC and on-prem deployments that codifies data residency and retention constraints and emits machine-readable evidence. The generator will produce per-customer deployment policies (region allow-lists, retention TTLs, encryption binding, and operational failover rules) and tie to the runtime control-plane checks used during routing and evacuation. This ticket focuses on the policy schema, enforcement hooks in the control plane, evidence collection format, and a small reference CLI to generate policies for onboarding customers with strict residency needs.
acceptance_criteria: Policy generator CLI produces a JSON policy for a sample customer that includes permitted regions, retention TTL (per data class), encryption key binding, and failover constraints with explicit holdback windows.

Control plane enforces region allow-list: any incoming request for a customer with a policy using 'region_allow_list' is routed only to nodes in allowed regions or rejected with a documented policy-violation response code.
Retention settings applied at storage layer: TTL markers emitted and evidence events logged when data is scheduled for deletion; log entries follow the evidence schema below.

Failover constraints enforced: automatic cross-region evacuation respects per-policy constraints (e.g., 'evacuation_allowed: false' or 'evacuation_min_time_hours') and triggers an operator alert if forced evacuation would violate policy.

Evidence/reporting automation: daily artifact generated (signed JSON) summarizing residency posture and retention actions for each active policy and stored to the compliance bucket with least-privilege ACLs.
Unit and integration tests covering generator, enforcement hook, and evidence emitter with mocked storage and routing layers.
Pull request with code, README, and a Confluence doc outlining the policy fields and operator runbook is merged and reviewed by Security and Compliance teams.

notes: Trade-offs: embedding strict regional failover prohibition improves compliance but increases outage blast radius and manual operator workload; we will allow configurable soft-fallback windows (evacuation_min_time_hours) to balance availability vs compliance.

Decision: use signed JSON policy files (ed25519) stored in customer-specific S3 buckets as the authoritative policy artifact; control plane caches signed policy with TTL and validates signature on refresh.
Scope exclusion: this ticket does not implement KMS/HSM integrations for key binding; that is a follow-up (see dependencies).
Performance: enforcement hook should add <2ms median overhead to routing path; we will measure in a canary before wide rollout.
audit_log_schema_summary: Each enforcement decision emits an audit event with fields: timestamp, policy_id, policy_signature, customer_id, request_id, routed_region, decision (allowed|blocked|deferred), reason_code, operator_override (if any). Events are batched hourly and signed before archival.
evidence_flow: 1) Policy generator emits signed policy file to customer bucket. 2) Control plane caches policy and validates per-request. 3) Storage layer emits TTL scheduling events when data class markers approach deletion; these events are recorded to the evidence stream. 4) Daily evidence aggregator compiles signed digest files (policy snapshot, deletion events, evacuation attempts) and uploads to the compliance artifact store. 5) Artifact retention follows customer-specified retention + platform retention floor.
rollback_plan: If enforcement causes customer outages during canary, we will revert the enforcement toggle for that customer (feature-flag off) and revert cached policies; operator runbook includes 'drain control-plane caches' and 'reissue signed no-op policy' to allow traffic while preserving audit trail.
